sections.content:
[piece, plus] still does nothing. That is, plus is not the target.
Let me reconsider. What are the remaining untested interactions?
- [piece, Ɔ] (grow) — tested on green: +2.
- [piece, U] — untested.
- [piece, the other piece] — untested!
- [cell, cell], [plus, plus], [cell, piece] (reverse order) — untested.
- Single clicks on everything — no effect.
- [piece, plus] — no effect (tested twice).
Maybe the goal is: shrink both pieces to a minimum, then [green piece, yellow piece] or vice versa? Or [piece, its own cell] to dock?
Let me think about the shape of the cell again:
- C: opens to the right. Ɔ: opens to the left.
- П: opens downward. U: opens upward.
Green piece: tab on the left. Yellow piece: cap on top.
Maybe docking: the piece enters the cell from the opening:
- Green (tab on left) enters C (opens right) from the right side? The piece's tab points left, and the cell's opening is on the right — the piece enters from the right, and the tab points left, toward the cell's back wall.
- Yellow (cap on top) enters П (opens downward) from below? The cap points up, and the cell's opening is at the bottom — the piece enters from below, and the cap points up, toward the top wall.
So the pairing: green→C, yellow→П.
But when I clicked [green, C] earlier, it shrank instead of docking. Maybe docking only works when the piece is at minimum size? Green is now at minimum (2 cells). Let me try [green, C] now!
Current green: rows 9-11, cols 27-28. Click (10,28), then click C (21,39).
Current yellow: rows 27-29, cols 9-11. Click (28,10), then click П (38,24).
Batch: (10,28), (21,39), (28,10), (38,24). Observe.
If docking works, the piece should move into the box or disappear.
